claim: At a field 1000 m above sea level, air density drops about 10%, raising stall speed above 14 m/s (margin is only 0.013 m/s at sea level) so stall_speed fails.

At a 3500 m field on a +45 K hot day the thinner, hotter air drops the pack-burst-limited hover T/W below 1.8, so hover_thrust_to_weight fails. The margin fell from 0.128 to 0.044 going from 1000 m/+15 K to 2000 m/+35 K.

At a 3000 m field on a +35 K day, hover current rises as air density falls. The 10 AWG lift ESC feed is already at 123 C steady at 51.6 A, with only 15.6 C of margin after a burst, so wire_temperature fails.

At a 3500 m field on a +45 K hot day the thinner, hotter air drops pack-burst-limited hover T/W below 1.8 and hover_thrust_to_weight fails (the margin fell 0.128 to 0.044 going from 1000 m/+15 K to 2000 m/+35 K).

At a 3000 m field on a +35 K day, hover current rises with the lower air density; the 10 AWG lift ESC feed is already at 123 C steady at 51.6 A with only 15.6 C of margin to the insulation limit after a burst, so wire_temperature fails.
